The Experience
Where the desert meets the river

The Orange River cuts through one of South Africa's most dramatic landscapes — arid, rocky, and utterly remote. Rocky mountains rise from the desert floor, and then the river appears, a ribbon of green and life running straight through terrain that looks like it belongs on another planet.


Vendy Fishing runs a fully guided, fully catered drift experience down a private 40km stretch of the Orange River. You will not see another person. You will have no signal. You will have nothing to think about except the water in front of you, the fish below the surface, and the people beside you around the fire at night.

"This is not a fishing trip. It is a reset. The river demands your full attention and rewards it completely."

The Orange River at dusk — pure wilderness

Getting There

The Itinerary
Day by Day
Arrival — Night 0
Base Camp
Arrive at a beautiful farmhouse — your base camp for the night before the drift begins. Full amenities, a braai under the stars, cold drinks, and the kind of conversation that only happens when phones go quiet. Your guides will brief you on the days ahead.
Days 1 — 4
The River
Morning: Wake at sunrise to coffee and a light breakfast on the bank. The guides rig the boats as the river turns gold.

On the water: Drift downstream — fishing the rapids, the pools, the shallows. Guides navigate, call fish, and put you in the right spot at the right time.

Midday: Your crew sets up a riverside lunch ahead of you. Rest, swim, explore. Hike to the mountain tops for views that don't exist anywhere else.

Evening: Camp is set up before you arrive. Fire, food, cold beers, and stories of the fish caught — and the bigger ones lost. Sleep under the stars.
Night 5
Back to Base
Return to the farmhouse for a hot shower, a last meal together, and the strange mix of exhaustion and elation that only a trip like this produces. Depart the following morning.
Camp on the banks — everything set up before you arrive
The Target Species
Chasing Yellowfish
"A fish of a thousand casts, a thousand stories, a thousand flies and a million dreams."
The Largemouth Yellowfish

The Yellowfish — Labeobarbus — is endemic to South Africa. You will not find them anywhere else in the world. The Orange River holds two species, and chasing both on the fly is one of the great freshwater experiences the country has to offer.

Smallmouth Yellowfish
Labeobarbus aeneus — "Smallies"
Abundant, hard fighting, and willing to smash a dry fly in the shallows when the river is at the right level. When conditions align — the water clear, the sun high — you can sight fish to individual fish holding in the current. Watch them take the fly. One of the great moments in freshwater fishing.
Abundant · Sight Fishing · All Techniques
Largemouth Yellowfish
Labeobarbus kimberleyensis — "Largies"
The fish of a thousand casts. Elusive, technical, and the bucket list target of every serious angler who has fished this river. Largies can grow to 30lbs and feed in lower light conditions. To land one on the fly is an achievement that stays with you. The unfinished chapter — always a reason to go back.
Elusive · Bucket List · Technical
All Yellowfish fishing is strictly catch and release
The Community
Shared Stories

The best part of the drift is not the fish — it is who you share it with. The Orange River strips away every distraction and leaves you fully present with the people around you. Some of the best conversations of your life happen around a campfire on this river.


Vendy Fishing welcomes groups of friends, family, and corporate teams. Whether you are an experienced fly fisher or picking up a rod for the first time, the river works for everyone.

"The fish of a thousand casts. But it's the stories around the fire that bring you back."
Smallmouth Yellowfish — endemic to South Africa
Beyond the Fishing
The River Life
Bird life: Fish Eagles, African Darters, Kingfishers, and numerous raptors — the Orange River corridor is extraordinary for birding
Mountain walks: Hike up from the river bank to views across the desert that stretch for kilometres
Swimming: A midday swim in a quiet pool is one of the great simple pleasures of the drift
Stargazing: Northern Cape darkness means a sky full of stars. Sleep without the tent roof and wake to the Milky Way
The campfire: Stories, cold beers, and conversation that only happens when there is nowhere else to be
Kingfisher — one of many species along the river corridor
When to Go
The Season

July through November is the prime window — clear water, predictable flows, and the fish actively feeding on the surface and in the shallows.


November is particularly special — the pre-rain period when Smallies are most aggressive and Largemouth are increasingly active as the days shorten. Winter months still produce good fishing with Largemouth more abundant in cooler, slower flows.


Fishing Techniques
Nymphing in the rapids — accessible to all levels
Dry fly and sight fishing in the shallows
Streamer fishing for larger Smallies
Technical low-light targeting of Largemouth
1 guide per 2 guests on the water at all times

Preparation
What to Bring
Clothing & Personal
Long-sleeve sun shirt (SPF)
Wide-brim hat
Polarised sunglasses
Wading shoes / sandals
Light fleece for evenings
Sleeping bag
Personal medications
Insect repellent
Headlamp
Pillow
Drinks & Extras
Bottled water (personal supply)
Beers, wine, spirits
Snacks for the boat
Cash for gratuities
Fly Fishing Gear
Rods: 5wt for Smallies, 7-8wt for Largemouth
Lines: Weight forward floating + sink tip for pools
Leaders: 3x-4x fluorocarbon
Dry flies: Stimulators, Elk Hair Caddis, Mayflies
Nymphs: Hare's Ear, Copper John, Woolly Buggers
Streamers: Clouser Minnow, small baitfish patterns
Net: Rubber mesh landing net
Dry bag: For gear on the boat

Good to Know
Before You Go
Conservation
All Yellowfish fishing is strictly catch and release. Barbless hooks strongly encouraged. We operate within the Kalahari Largemouth Yellowfish Conservancy guidelines — protecting this fishery for future generations.
Fitness & Ability
No special fitness required. Most fishing is done from the drift boats. Optional walks and wading at your own pace. The trip suits beginners and experienced fly fishers alike.
Insurance & Safety
Comprehensive travel and medical insurance required. All guides trained in river safety and first aid. Medical evacuation coverage strongly recommended for remote wilderness activities.
